entities.name: Clare of Assisi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Chiara Offreduccio, known as Clare of Assisi, was an Italian saint and one of the first followers of Francis of Assisi, born in Assisi, Italy around 1194. She founded the Poor Clares Order and lived a life of extreme poverty and devotion to God, dying on August 18, 1253, at the age of 59. Clare's legacy extends to the establishment of the Dominican Order and her influence on the development of Franciscan spirituality, with her writings and teachings continuing to inspire religious orders and reform movements to this day. Her feast day, October 11, is celebrated by Catholics worldwide, and her life has been the subject of numerous artistic and literary works, including the famous frescoes by Giotto in the Basilica of San Francesco in Assisi. As the founder of the Poor Clares, Clare's contributions to the reform of the Catholic Church and the establishment of new religious orders have had a lasting impact on the history of Christianity. Through her example of radical poverty and devotion, Clare has inspired countless individuals and communities to re-examine their relationship with God and the world around them.
